newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka stocks end up, held back by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka stocks end up, held back by profit-taking.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up on Wednesday, but the momentum was slowed down by retail profit-taking, analysts said.
The all share index closed two points up at 806.2. Price gains outnumbered losses by 44 to 27. Aitken Spence & Co rose 15 rupees to 200, John Keells Holdings five to 305.
"The index was up by about seven points in early trading, but profit-taking by retailers slowed it down," said Shanil Perera of brokerage Lanka Securities.
"The index should stay firm as retailers return with profits and because the market is moving on fundamentals," Perera added.

Turnover, led by foreign buying was 169.8 million rupees. The main trades were 500,000 Agalawatte Plantations, 100,000 Development Finance, 107,100 Pelwatte Sugar, 130,000 Royal Ceramic, 300,000 Sampath Bank.
Foreign buying was worth 95.5 million rupees while selling was 15.4 milion.
There are bargains to pick in Colombo despite the index having gained over 30 percent this year, analysts said.

"There are bargains if you have research that can point you in the right direction," said Nihal Dissanayake, general manager of National Asset Management (NAMAL). NAMAL is launching a growth fund on June 30 which will invest 90 percent of its value in the share market.
